episodes.title: A Cult Psychologist Explains Why So Many Fell For, and Remain Addicted to Trump.
episodes.description:
I spent seven years on The Farm — the world's largest hippie commune — as an enthusiastic, missionary-zeal true believer. I wasn't a cult member exactly, but I was decidedly cultish. This talk, given at the International Cultic Studies Association conference in San Diego, is my attempt to explain why: not through coercive control, but through what I call "heart purging" — the very human appetite for unearned, unconditional self-confidence that cults offer for free.

Working alongside Harvard biological anthropologist Terrence Deacon for the past 30 years, I've tried to build a fully physical explanation of motivation, selfhood, and interpretation — no skipped steps, no unexplained "black box" concepts borrowed from folk psychology. I call this natural naming, as opposed to the intuitive naming that dominates most of the social sciences (and most of cultic studies).

In this talk I connect that framework to absolutism itself — the oldest and, I'd argue, the biggest unsolved threat to human survival. I lay out:

- The difference between intuitive naming (reifying vague concepts like "motivation" or "information") and natural naming (explaining form and function from chemistry on up)
- Why cults are best understood as proprietary lifestyle brands selling a universal human product: unconditional, unearned self-confidence
- "Mojonomics" — the behavioral economics of self-confidence, and why we compete for it like a black-market currency
- A natural-naming explanation of the Dark Triad (narcissism, Machiavellianism, psychopathy) as a kind of "playing God"
- Why coercive control explains how cults operate, but heart purging explains why we let them

If you've ever wondered how intelligent, decent people end up devoted to absolutist causes — political, religious, or otherwise — this is my attempt at an answer grounded in biology rather than blame.

2:05 My Seven Years on The Farm Commune
5:40 Missionary Zeal and "I Once Was Lost, But Now I'm Blind"
7:50 Meeting Terrence Deacon and the Turn to Evolutionary Epistemology
10:45 Absolutism: Humanity's Oldest Unsolved Threat (AI Dialogue)
15:20 Intuitive Naming: How Science Reifies the Unexplained
20:10 Wildcard Trump Cards and the Supernatural
22:45 Natural Naming: The Donut, Form, and Matter
26:15 How Life Began: Self-Regenerating Form
28:50 Homo Sapiens as "FOMO Escapians": Language and Symbols
32:20 Mojonomics: The Economics of Self-Confidence
36:15 Sato-Narcissism and the Confidence Wars
39:10 Why I Loved the Commune: Heart Purging vs. Coercive Control
42:05 The Confidence Crisis and Cults as Free Confidence
44:35 The Dark Triad Explained Through Natural Naming
46:50 Conclusion: Building Immunity to Absolutism

#Cults #Absolutism #CulticStudies #Psychology #DarkTriad #Narcissism #CriticalThinking #TerrenceDeacon #Philosophy #SelfConfidence

This presentation from the 2026 International Cultic Studies Association conference examines the psychological architecture behind belief systems. By breaking down intuitive naming and heart-purging, the discussion offers a framework for understanding why individuals seek meaning through rigid structures. It is essential viewing for those interested in the intersection of psychology, sociology, and the mechanics of human behavior.

Rather than viewing these concepts in isolation, the session connects them to a physical explanation of existence. We analyze the view of God as an infinitely-optimized being to clarify how cultic studies help us decode complex patterns of motivation. Whether you are a researcher or someone curious about the roots of absolutism, this breakdown provides a clear academic perspective on the human condition.

episodes.title: Pt. 2 Jeremy Sherman live! Id-sercise! Because Morality Fails To Stop Moralizing Cults
episodes.description:
I'm Jeremy Sherman, PhD, a strategic consultant since 1997, specializing in dealing with jerks and doubts. 

For a free trial session, email me at js@jeremysherman.com
𝐅𝐚𝐜𝐞𝐛𝐨𝐨𝐤: facebook.com/jeremysherm

DEALING WITH JERKS
jerkology.net
BLOG: https://www.psychologytoday.com/us/blog/jerkology
BOOK: What's Up With A**holes? How to spot and stop them without becoming one. 
https://a.co/d/6QDQwrY
AUDIOBOOK: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iLerthdU4Jw&t

DEALING WITH DOUBTS
adaptivestrategies.net
BLOG: https://www.psychologytoday.com/us/blog/ambigamy
BOOK: Negotiate with Yourself and Win: Doubt Management Skills for People Who Can Hear Themselves Think: https://a.co/d/brJpNli

Though informal, I'll argue that my approach is more scientific than what passes for science. It is really abstract engineering researchers claiming we've got this or that add-on feature without explaining how we got it. That makes for excellent engineering, but it's no more rigorous than supernatural explanations. 

For 27 years, I've worked closely with Harvard/Berkeley biologist/neuroscientist Terrence Deacon on developing fully scientific explanations for phenomena assumed by other researchers. 

Some examples:

LIFE'S STRUGGLE FOR EXISTENCE: DNA and natural selection don't explain it. We have an entirely natural explanation for how self-regenerating beings (like us) could emerge from chemistry and evolve (by natural selection) the capacity to use DNA molecules.  

MOTIVATION: Psychologists just assume it. When they see effort, they assume a motivation, which is like assuming a "soul." We have an explanation for what effort and motivation physically are: Not something added to chemistry but the way chemistry can limit itself by channeling energy into work to regenerate itself. 

NARCISSISM: Psychologists say that if you've got these symptoms, you have a thing called Narcissism. I explain how humans, having evolved language, can imagine the ideal, see where we fall short, and self-idealize to compensate. It's something we all do. I study how it gets out of hand and becomes addictive.

My book on our research: Neither Ghost Nor Machine: The Emergence and Nature of Selves (Columbia University Press, 2017) https://a.co/d/9ZNyT7E

My PhD is in decision science. I'm a soulnerd with a deeply connected heart and head. This stuff is my non-spiritual path. I live and breathe my work. It's not some abstract intellectual exercise. 

Nor is it art. Science is a campaign to find natural explanations for all natural phenomena – natural, not supernatural - about which you can believe anything.

Still, I try to make this stuff fun, intuitive, and useful. I've written over 1,100 blog articles for Psychology Today on practical decision-making and everything we all go through (11 million views). Their editor-in-chief calls it, "Mind candy for people who aren't afraid to think."
